meta.rootTitle: Politicas — the empirical record of the republic
meta.rootDescription: Votes, public money, budgets and laws fused into one methodology-transparent effectiveness index for every Czech politician. Every number cites its open data source.
meta.dashboardDescription: Chamber overview: composite scores, the ranking, events in the public-money graph, and entry points to five tools.
meta.votetrackDescription: A ledger of roll-call votes, the chamber view and parliamentary-group discipline — three perspectives over psp.cz data. Feeds the Activity, Attendance and Independence pillars.
meta.moneyDescription: Public contracts, subsidies and donations traced through firms to politicians — an entity graph, a ledger of evidenced ties, and the trail methodology. Feeds the Integrity pillar.
meta.budgetDescription: A town's finances against similarly sized peers: debt per capita, capital-spending share and balance, from MONITOR / State Treasury data.
meta.lawwatchDescription: What actually changed in the law: section-by-section diffs linked to roll-call votes, and the legislative pipeline of House prints.
meta.civicscoreDescription: All 200 MPs by composite effectiveness score: the chamber distribution, the full ranking with a party filter, and a head-to-head of two MPs pillar by pillar.
meta.profileDescription: Composite score {score}/100 ({party}, {region}): pillars, roll-call votes and evidenced money ties. Every number cites its open source.
meta.rentgenDescription: Archived art direction of Politicas: an X-ray of the state — the money-trail graph, an audit log and a source register.
meta.graphDescription: A searchable knowledge graph of Czech politics: people, companies, public money, votes and laws in one network, every node linked to its register.
meta.metodikaDescription: The six components of the contribution index, their published weights, the saturation caps and the formula ref — rendered from the code that computes the score.
meta.exhibitDescription: A citable imprint of a control-room slice: content addressed by a content hash, with sources, the imprint and the data-retrieval date in the citation footer.
meta.graphCitationDescription: A permanent citation of one view of the Czech-politics knowledge graph: the claims, the human-review state of every edge, the sources and the content fingerprint at the moment of issue.
meta.krajDescription: Pick a region and get its MPs' slate: contribution index, components, badges — with source and date, ready to print.
meta.krajCardDescription: The MP slate ({count}): {kraj}. Contribution index from open psp.cz data, with source and date, ready to print.
meta.plakatDescription: The print form of the contribution-index leaderboard: an A4/A3 sheet with an archival citation footer (source, data state, methodology).
meta.moneyMpDescription: The full evidence chain of MP↔company ties — contracts, subsidies, donations, corroboration in ARES VR.
meta.moneyPacketDescription: An MP's case file compiled into a citable packet — human-verified ties only, a timeline, registry links and ready-made citation blocks. Excluded unverified material is disclosed.
meta.moneyCompanyDescription: A company as a crossroads of the graph — every MP tied to it, each tie's class and review state, and the company's contracts with the state.
meta.kauzyDescription: Hand-curated investigative dossiers (cases) — a dated, cited research trail split into what the sources establish and what they do not. Always pending review, never a confirmed accusation.
meta.kontrolaDescription: The review console for unconfirmed MP↔company ties — the evidence folder and deep links into the primary registers. The human gate: only a human can confirm a tie.
meta.stretyDescription: Deterministically computed conflict-of-interest candidates: an MP's vote on a print amending a statute that governs the public-money channel of a company where the registry records they held a role on the vote day. The time overlap is a fact; every candidate requires human verification — nothing here is an accusation.
meta.budgetMirrorDescription: The finances of any of Czechia's 6,254 municipalities against municipalities of similar size: debt per capita, capital-spending share, balance from FIN 2-12 M statements in the MONITOR system, and the municipality's money trail in the Contracts Register — with a computed peer group and openly stated coverage.
meta.budgetIcoDescription: The finances of {town} ({kraj}) against municipalities of similar size — debt per capita, capital-spending share and balance from FIN 2-12 M statements in the MONITOR system.
meta.lawCollisionsDescription: An early-warning system for the legislative process: a chronological ledger of findings (collisions of concurrently pending prints over the same section, derived conflict flags on sponsors) with permanent anchors, citation blocks and an RSS/JSON feed — plus clusters of case ③ close-read findings by act and section.
meta.lawStatuteRegistryDescription: Critical editions of Czech acts: who changed which statute, with a verbatim section trail from e-Sbírka where the archive carries one.
meta.lawStatuteTitle: Act No. {ref} Sb. — statute memory — Politicas
meta.lawStatuteDescription: The critical edition of Act No. {ref} Sb.: who changed it, with a verbatim section trail from e-Sbírka.
meta.kompasDescription: A reversed election calculator: take positions on real roll-call votes of the Chamber and compute — deterministically, from the stored PSP10 roll-call ballots — which MPs and groups voted like you. The result lives in the link, no account needed.

record.methodBody: Group line = strict majority of the group's positional ballots (for/against) in a given roll call; a tie determines no line. Discipline = share of the group's positional ballots on the line. Cohesion = the Rice index |for−against|/(for+against), weighted at chamber level by the positional-ballot counts of groups with ≥ 5 positional ballots. Since amendment 90/1995 Coll. the Chamber does not distinguish the “abstained / did not vote” slot and it does not count as a position; voided roll calls are excluded; unaffiliated MPs are displayed but not scored. The left-to-right ordering of groups in the hemicycle is an editorial constant.

kompas.title: Election compass, inverted
kompas.lead: Ordinary election calculators measure promises. This compass measures deeds: you take positions on real roll-call votes of the Chamber — and from the stored ballots it deterministically computes which MPs and groups voted like you. Every number links to the vote record.
kompas.howTo: FOR means voting for the motion exactly as it was put to the floor (the name is the literal vote title from psp.cz); AGAINST means voting against it. Skip a question you have no opinion on — it does not enter the computation.

kompas.selectionRule: Question selection rule: candidates are valid (non-voided) PSP10 roll-call votes with a theme from the vote_tag silver layer, excluding the Procedure and Other themes, with at least {minPositional} positional ballots (for + against). Within each theme, candidates are sorted by closeness |for−against|/(for+against) ascending (most divided first; ties: more positional ballots, more recent date, higher id). Themes are sorted by candidate count and the set is drawn round-robin — each theme's first pick, then the second — at most {perTheme} per theme and {cap} in total. The same record always yields the same questions.
kompas.scoringRule: Match rule: a roll call is comparable where the MP voted for/against; a match = their position equals yours. An MP's match = matches ÷ comparable votes. Since amendment 90/1995 Coll. the Chamber does not distinguish the “abstained / did not vote” slot — it counts neither as agreement nor disagreement and does not enter the denominator; absence does not either (both are shown separately). Only MPs with a positional ballot on at least half of your answered questions enter the ranking. Groups are measured the same way against their line (strict majority of the group's positional ballots).

rules.r2: A roll call enters only if it is not voided and links deterministically to a print: primarily through the session agenda (psp.cz bod_schuze — session + agenda item → print), as a fallback through a print number in its title. An agenda item covering several prints at once (joint debate) is conservatively skipped and counted separately — no candidate is ever built on an ambiguous key.
rules.r3: A print enters only if the graph records it amending at least one statute from the disclosed relevance table below, matched to the public-money channels that company actually has.
rules.r4: The vote day must lie inside the registry-confirmed role period — both boundary days inclusive.
rules.r5: Only a positional ballot (yes/no) forms a candidate; abstentions and absences never do.
rules.r6: One candidate per (tie × vote); several affected statutes merge into that one row.

dependency.aside: {billsFmt} prints · {hitsFmt} dependency findings · print texts on psp.cz
dependency.intro: The detector walks each print’s own text looking for the e-Sbírka drafting placeholder (“zákona č. …/2026 Sb.”), which a drafter inserts into amending sentences before the final act number is known. Each hit falls into one of three classes — the print cites its own later act, the print relies on ANOTHER, companion print that must pass at the same time or earlier, or the hit remains unclear because the available text carries no evidence for either of the first two. The classification was manually audited; even so, {unclearFmt} of {totalFmt} hits honestly remain unclear and are not rendered below. A dependency on a companion print is a fact of the legislative process — it flags an enactment-order risk (this print assumes the companion print will already be law), not an accusation of wrongdoing.

metodika.capCommittee: distinct committees, commissions and delegations at which committee work already pays its full weight
metodika.capLegislative: bills and interpellations combined at which legislative output already pays its full weight
metodika.capSpeech: floor turns at which the speech component already pays its full weight
metodika.capsLead: Three components rest on counts rather than ratios, and a count grows without a ceiling. The saturation point is the value above which the component already pays its full weight - otherwise one exceptionally talkative MP would move the scale for the whole chamber.
metodika.dedupeHeading: Committees are counted by body, not by row
metodika.dedupeLead: psp.cz files a body an MP leads as TWO membership rows - the membership itself and the function. Counting rows therefore let chairing one committee outrank sitting on two. The index has counted distinct bodies since; role weighting is unchanged and lives in its own leadership component.
metodika.dedupeUnknownOrgan: A row whose body identifier is missing is merged with nothing: no other row can be proven to be the same body, and merging on a guess would quietly remove points.
metodika.lead: The contribution index is a transparent weighted sum over six components psp.cz publishes. This page is not a prose restatement of the formula — its figures are read straight from the code that computes the score, so changing a weight or a saturation cap reflows the page. What is not here is not part of the index.
metodika.ratesLead: The remaining three components are ratios: voting participation is the share of roll calls at which the MP took a position; attendance is the complement of the excused-day share; leadership is binary - an MP who leads at least one body earns the whole weight.
metodika.refHeading: The formula ref, and what the data says about itself
metodika.refLead: The formula has a name. Every writer that stores a score stamps this ref on the MP node, so it can be compared against what actually authored the stored numbers - and that is exactly the difference that stayed invisible for six days between 2026-07-29 and 2026-08-04.

meta.description: A chronological daily record of the state: signed contracts, prints referred to committees, promulgations in the Collection of Laws, register roles and human-gate decisions — dated, cited, permanently linkable.

denik.kicker: the daily record of the republic
denik.title: Journal of the Republic
denik.lead: One day, one entry: contracts signed by companies tied to MPs, parliamentary prints referred to committees, promulgations in the Collection of Laws, register-role entries and removals, and human-gate decisions. Every row has a date and a source, and every day has a permanent address.

rule.body: The journal runs two streams, and every row states which clock dates it. effective rows carry the day the event happened according to its register (a contract signature, a role entry, a print step) — not the day ingest found it. recorded rows carry the day the fact entered the record: human-gate decisions (review_audit is an append-only log) and, since the bitemporal graph arrived, changes of the graph itself (change_event — a new tie, a tie change, a contract in the graph). What the graph recorded before the bitemporal-migration epoch, the “recorded” stream honestly does not carry — nothing is stamped retroactively. Contracts are listed only for companies with an owner/operator-class tie — contracts of institutions where an MP merely sits on a body are that institution's money.

hero.title: Civic Inbox
hero.lead: Follow MPs, bills, companies or municipalities — and on every visit the inbox shows you what changed in the record since the previous one. Every row is a dated journal entry with its source; the inbox adds nothing, it only filters.

rule.body1: Following works without an account: the list lives in your browser (localStorage). When news is requested, though, that whole list travels in the request ADDRESS (?e=poslanec:…) — that is by design, because the address is also your subscription: it can be saved or passed on, and whoever has it sees the same selection. No cookies, no sign-in, nothing stored on the server; the keys are struck from server telemetry and only their count remains. What the server sees, as with any other page, is the request IP address — the inbox does not remove that and does not claim otherwise. Journal entries are dated by day, so the “since your last visit” threshold is daily: the day of the last visit is counted whole again — better to show an entry twice than to withhold one.
rule.firstVisit: A first visit has no stamp — the last {days} days of the record are shown.
rule.body2: The badge in the sidebar follows a stricter rule: after a visit the inbox notes how many of that day's entries you had in front of you, and the badge then leaves them out — which is why it goes dark after a visit even though the visit day still counts whole above the threshold. Only the count from that same day is subtracted; nothing else. The page stays lenient — the two rules differ on purpose.
rule.body3: What the inbox CANNOT see: for the contribution index recompute it reports only THAT it ran — the graph holds only current values and no previous ones, so how far a score moved cannot be derived from it and the inbox does not claim it. The row therefore carries the pass number, the formula ref and a link to the <metodika>methodology</metodika>. It is reported only when the whole chamber holds one pass; half a recompute is not a fact. The kind summary in an entity header counts the whole delta, even when only the first {cap} rows fit below it.

meta.title: Open Data Quality Atlas — Politicas
meta.description: Public quality grades for the sources politicas ingests: provenance coverage, freshness against cadence, Merkle seal integrity, completeness measured by admitted gaps. Every score ships with its rule printed next to it; a dimension without evidence is “unrated”, never zero.

hero.kicker: the public quality atlas of the data layer’s sources
hero.title: Open Data Quality Atlas
hero.lead: Every source politicas ingests gets a public grade here: provenance coverage, freshness against its declared cadence, the integrity of Merkle seals, and completeness measured by upstream’s admitted gaps. Every score carries its rule printed verbatim next to the number — and a dimension without evidence is honestly “unrated”, never zero. The traps you will run into here (sentinel birth dates, merged K votes, placeholder years 2925) are the same institutional memory that politicas’ analytical runs read.

methodology.body: Scores 0–100 are computed deterministically from the current state of the store (entity tables with the provenance quartet, the ingest_run table, source contexts). Cadence vocabulary: age of the last refresh ≤ cadence is “fresh”, up to {stale}× cadence “aging”, beyond {stale}× cadence “stale”; the freshness score falls to zero at {zero}× cadence. Cadence is politicas’ declared expectation, not the publisher’s SLA. Low completeness is a statement about the publisher’s data, not about the processing — gaps are admitted, not hidden. A dimension without evidence is “unrated” with a reason and does not enter the composite.

cards.sortRule: sorting rule: descending by the chosen score; “unrated” always sorts after rated — unrated is not zero even when sorting; ties are decided by the source key

coverage.label: provenance coverage
coverage.rule: 100 × (source rows linked to an ingest run / all source rows in the store), rounded. A row without ingest_run_id carries only partial provenance (source + url + fetched_at); a row with it is traceable back to the run that wrote it. A source with no rows = unrated.

freshness.label: freshness
freshness.rule: Age = today minus the finish of the source’s last successful ingest run. Score 100 at age ≤ cadence, then linear to 0 at age = 3× cadence. In words: ≤ cadence is “fresh”, ≤ 2× cadence “aging”, beyond 2× cadence “stale”. Cadence is politicas’ declared expectation, not the publisher’s SLA. Without a declared cadence or a successful run = unrated.

integrity.label: integrity
integrity.rule: 100 × (the source’s finished successful runs sealed with a Merkle root / all of the source’s finished successful runs), rounded. The seal is applied by LedgerRepository.sealIngestRun over every row the run wrote. A source with no finished successful run = unrated.

completeness.label: completeness
completeness.rule: 100 minus 10 points for every admitted upstream gap (KNOWN ISSUES in the source context, lib/analysis/context-model.ts), floored at 0. A low score is a statement about the publisher’s data, not about politicas’ processing — gaps are admitted, not hidden. A source without a processed context = unrated (undocumented ≠ complete).

hero.title: Data Releases
hero.lead: The graph of the republic is released like software: every successful data ingest cuts a <mono>YYYY.MM.DD</mono> version, cardinality floors are the release gate, and the integrity of every release is provable by Merkle roots and the review hash-chain. What you download today you can cite — and anyone can verify it.

methodology.body: Version = the day of the last finished successful ingest run (the ingest_run table). A version that misses the cardinality floors (CARDINALITY_FLOORS) is marked “degraded” and is never “latest”. Floor verdicts are computed from the current state of the store — about historical versions this page claims nothing it could not prove. The snapshot is a cut of the derived graph (kg_node / kg_edge) capped at {nodeCap} nodes and {edgeCap} edges; any truncation is admitted in the limits field.

feeds.title: Feeds
feeds.aside: source: the application’s route handlers — {count} public addresses
feeds.lead: {families} feed families, each in two formats: {formats}. The JSON shape is the same wire for all of them — you can validate it with a single validator (<mono>parseEvidenceFeedJson</mono>). A feed never returns emptiness in place of a failure: if the store is unreadable it answers <mono>503</mono>, because an empty list is the claim “nothing happened”.
feeds.machineTitle: machine shapes that are not feeds
feeds.sitemap: The page map for robots is published by <mono>/sitemap.xml</mono>, crawling rules by <mono>/robots.txt</mono>. The sitemap carries static surfaces; the addresses of individual MPs, prints and companies are deliberately not in it — enumerating them means reading the whole graph at request time, and the hub pages that lead to them are in the sitemap.

denik.title: Journal of the Republic
denik.carries: dated records of the state — signed contracts of companies that MPs own or manage, prints referred to committees, promulgations in the Collection of Laws, registry role entries and removals, human-gate decisions and records of changes in the graph.
denik.note: the last {count} records; the ?entita='<klíč>' parameter (poslanec:'<id>' · firma:'<ičo>' · tisk:'<číslo>') narrows the feed to a single entity — the address IS the subscription.

dukazy.title: Evidence Journal
dukazy.carries: human-gate decisions over MP↔company ties — what was confirmed, rejected and returned for more evidence, each a link of the hash-chain.
dukazy.note: reviewers’ notes are not published; the feed carries the decision, not its reasoning.

kolize.title: Collision Radar
kolize.carries: candidates for a conflict of interest between a sponsored print and a money tie of its sponsor.
kolize.note: a radar hit is a signal to investigate, not a proven conflict — every row carries that with it.

schranka.title: News for followed entities
schranka.carries: the same records, but only about the entities you follow — plus recalculations of your MP’s contribution index.
schranka.note: the feed is parametrized and follows nothing without parameters: the entity list is passed as ?e='<klíč>' (repeatable) and the day threshold as ?od=YYYY-MM-DD. Nothing is stored on the server and no identity is sent — the /schranka page builds the address itself and the keys are scrubbed from telemetry. The server still sees the request’s IP, though.

novinky.title: News — badge response
novinky.carries: the same deltas as the inbox feed, but in the shape the app’s bar reads; it is not a JSON Feed.

privacy.title: Privacy Notice
privacy.lead: Politicas publishes scored data about Members of the Czech Parliament compiled exclusively from public registries. This document describes what is processed, on what legal basis, and what rights you have — whether you are a visitor or a scored public official.
privacy.s1Body: The controller of the personal data published on this platform is the operator: [PROVOZOVATEL — doplnit před spuštěním / OPERATOR — fill in before launch]. Until the operator's identity is filled in, this page cannot be considered complete information under Articles 13 and 14 GDPR.
privacy.s2Lead: The platform processes and publishes data about Members of Parliament — public officials in the exercise of their mandate. All of it comes from publicly accessible sources:
privacy.s2SourcePsp: Chamber of Deputies (psp.cz) — mandates, votes, speeches, body memberships
privacy.s2SourceContracts: Czech Contract Registry (Registr smluv) — contracts of obligated entities
privacy.s2SourceAres: ARES and the Commercial Register — company roles and ownership ties
privacy.s2SourceLaws: Collection of Laws (Sbírka zákonů) — statutes and legislative traces
privacy.s2Purpose: The purpose of processing is transparency of public power: making what is already public accessible in a structured form, together with a documented scoring method. We do not process data from MPs' private lives — only data relating to the exercise of public office and to roles recorded in public registries.
privacy.s2LegalBasis: The legal basis is the legitimate interest in scrutiny of public power under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR, in the context of processing for journalistic purposes and purposes of academic, artistic or literary expression under Article 85 GDPR and Sections 17 et seq. of Czech Act No. 110/2019 Coll. This summary describes the operator's position, is not legal advice, and its final wording must be reviewed by the operator before launch.
privacy.s3Lead: The platform does not track visitors. It stores only functional cookies, without which the language choice and the operator console would not work:
privacy.s3CookieLocale: NEXT_LOCALE — the chosen interface language (Czech/English). Valid for 1 year. Set only once you pick a language.
privacy.s3CookieAdmin: politicas_admin — the access cookie of the /admin operator console. HttpOnly, scoped to the /admin path, valid for 12 hours. It is never set for a regular visitor — it concerns the operator only.
privacy.s3Analytics: Traffic may be measured with Plausible — cookieless, with no identification of individuals. Measurement is active only when the operator deploys it; without configuration, the script is not loaded at all.
privacy.s3Sentry: Error reports may be sent to Sentry (technical error context, not behavioural tracking). This too is active only when deployed by the operator; without configuration, nothing is sent.
privacy.s3NoTracking: No ad tracking, no profiling of visitors, no sharing of visitor data with third parties for marketing.
privacy.s4Body: Everyone whose data the platform publishes — including the scored MPs — has the right of access, the right to rectification of inaccurate data, and the right to object to processing based on legitimate interest (Articles 15, 16 and 21 GDPR). You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection (uoou.gov.cz).
privacy.s4Correction: The correction path is part of the method: every published figure links to the verification page, where a number can be checked against its source and a discrepancy can be reported.
privacy.s4NoContact: The operator's contact address will be added together with the operator's identity above.
privacy.s5Body: Public-registry data is retained for as long as it is published on the platform. The scoring method is versioned and corrections are never silent — the history of corrections and method versions is documented on the methodology page. Visitor data is not retained beyond the cookie lifetimes described above.
